..
Issued at 300 AM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

Currently-Today... KMLB radar imagery shows mostly dry weather 
across east central Florida with isolated showers from southern 
Brevard county southwards. GOES-19 satellite imagery and local 
observations generally indicate partly cloudy skies across east 
central Florida. Temperatures are currently in the low 70s to low 
80s with dew points in the low to upper 70s. Analysis charts show a 
mid/upper level high (591mb) over the state of Florida and the 
western Atlantic.  

Isolated to numerous showers (20-60% chance) and lightning storms 
forecast to develop in the afternoon and evening hours with south-
southeast low level flow in place and daytime heating. The greatest 
chance (40-60%) for showers and lightning storms are expected to be 
over areas along and north of I-4 as outflow from showers/storms
upstream of east central Florida converge with southeasterly flow.
The highest chance for showers and lightning storms is between 
2PM and 8PM before rain chances gradually diminish across northern
east central Florida tonight. Guidance shows MLCAPE up to 
500-3,100 J/kg, 0-6km shear up to 5-25kts, PWATs up to 2.0-2.4", 
and 500mb temperatures at around -6C. Thus, the potential exists 
for isolated strong storms capable of occasional to frequent 
lightning, wind gusts up to 35-45mph, and heavy rainfall (up to 
1-3" in 60 minutes). Afternoon highs in the upper 80s to low 90s 
with heat index values up to 98F-106F degrees are forecast. There 
is a Moderate HeatRisk with areas of Major HeatRisk, especially 
near the Orlando metro. A Moderate HeatRisk affects those 
sensitive to heat without adequate cooling and hydration; a Major 
HeatRisk affects anyone without adequate cooling and hydration. 
Remember to practice heat safety, such as taking breaks in air 
conditioned air and drink plenty of water! 

Monday-Tuesday... A cold front is forecast to move southeast across 
the Deep South and northern Florida to start off the workweek before 
stalling across east central Florida on Tuesday. Scattered to 
numerous showers (30-70% chance) and lightning storms are forecast 
to develop along and ahead of the front across east central Florida 
into the afternoon and evening hours on Monday. The greatest chance 
for rain showers and lightning storms is between 2PM and 2AM. Above 
normal rain chances (80-90%) are forecast on Tuesday with the front 
expected to stall over the middle of east central Florida. ECMWF and 
NAEFS ensembles show PWAT values (2.0"+) towards the 99th+ 
percentile for both days. Additionally, guidance indicates moderate 
instability/CAPE values, weak to moderate bulk shear, and relatively 
warm 500mb temperatures. The aforementioned weather parameters is 
likely to limit the stronger storm potential, especially when 
coupled with substantial cloud cover; however, flooding will be a 
concern with slow storm motions and repeated rounds of showers/ 
storms expected. For this reason, the WPC has placed all of east 
central Florida in a Marginal Risk (level 1 out of 5) for excessive 
rainfall on Tuesday. The primary hazards with a couple to a few 
strong storms will be occasional to frequent lightning, wind 
gusts up to 40-50mph, and heavy rainfall resulting in flooding 
(~5% chance) of roadways, as well as low-lying areas. Temperatures
will be dependent on exactly where the front meanders with 
afternoon highs in the mid 80s to low 90s forecast on Monday 
expected to reduce to the low 80s to near 90F degrees on Tuesday. 
Heat index values in the mid 90s to around 103F degrees are 
forecast on Monday with the upper 80s to around 100F degrees on 
Tuesday forecast. A Moderate HeatRisk exists on Monday. 

Wednesday-Saturday... Deterministic models and LREF-clusters are 
in good agreement that a longwave trough will deepen over the Deep
south through Wednesday before the Atlantic ridge builds back 
over the state of Florida Thursday into Friday. A continuation of 
a blocking pattern is expected to keep the stationary boundary 
over east central Florida through at least Friday with high 
pressure upstream over the Ohio Valley/northeastern US, as well as
high pressure downstream over the western Atlantic. Above normal 
rain chances (~70-90% chance) are forecast each day with scattered
to numerous/widespread showers and lightning storms forecast, 
especially in the afternoon/evening hours. Grounds are expected to
already be saturated at this point due to previous rains, and 
therefore flooding will continue to be a concern each day. It'll 
also take less rainfall to result in flooding by this point 
coupled with slow storm motions and repeated rounds of showers and
lightning storms. For this reason, the WPC has place all of east 
central Florida in a Marginal Risk (level 1 out of 5) for 
excessive rainfall on Wednesday. Expect below normal to seasonable
high temperatures and generally near normal low temperatures.
